title: Customer support and success
description: Prepare the support and customer success teams to answer, diagnose and measure the change once customers use it.
expertises: Ticket triage, escalation and service levels
questions: What will customers ask about this change, and where will support find the answer?
Which problems can support solve alone, and which go to engineering with what information?
How will tickets and feedback show that the change works for customers?

sources.title: Consortium for Service Innovation, Knowledge-Centered Success (KCS)
ISO 10002, Customer satisfaction, guidelines for complaints handling
ISO 18295-1:2017, Customer contact centres, requirements for customer contact centres

specialists.title: Support readiness lead
specialists.focus: List the questions and errors customers will raise and check that support has an article, a macro or a script for each before release.
checks: Each expected question or error has an article, macro or script before release.
Agents can see the customer's state needed to diagnose the problem.

specialists.title: Escalation manager
specialists.focus: Define what support collects before escalating, who receives the escalation and the response time for each severity.
checks: The data support collects before escalating is listed.
Each severity has a recipient and a response time.

specialists.title: Knowledge manager
specialists.focus: Plan the knowledge base articles to create or update, their owner and how agents improve them from real tickets.
checks: Articles to create or update have an owner and name the version they apply to.
Articles are improved from real tickets after release.

specialists.title: Customer success manager
specialists.focus: Identify the accounts most affected and how adoption or dissatisfaction will show in usage, tickets and renewals.
checks: The most affected accounts are listed with their owner.
Usage, ticket and renewal signals to watch are named.

evidence: Current top ticket categories and volumes for the area the change touches.
Draft knowledge base articles, macros or troubleshooting steps for the change.
Escalation path, severity definitions and service level commitments in force.
Accounts or segments most affected and the success metric to follow after release.
challenge: What is the first ticket we will receive after release, and can support answer it without engineering?
Which error message or state would a customer report in words support cannot link to a cause?
Does the release date leave support time to train before customers see the change?
Which signal would show that customers struggle before they churn or complain?
decision_criteria: Proceed when support has the articles, escalation path and training it needs before customers see the change.
Revise when error messages, logs or admin tools do not let support diagnose the likely problems.
Ask for a support briefing or a staged rollout when ticket volume could exceed the team's service levels.
Name the metric and threshold that will show whether the change reduced or increased support load.
